text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Unemployment benefits will be raised to 80 percent from 75 percent from October, under an agreement between the government, the umbrella union body LO and the Centre party. Union members' monthly payments into an unemployemnt fund will be raised by about 20 crowns. The agreement also proposes a time limit for how long unemployment benefits will be paid.

- Scandinavian Airline Systems SAS is part of a new alliance involving nine airlines that has been set up to counteract competition from an alliance between British Airways and American Airlines. The new alliance involves Lufthansa, United Airlines, Air Canada, and Thai International.

- Boliden, the mining and metals units of Trelleborg, is to be listed in Toronto later this year and half of its shares sold off. Analysts estimate Boliden to be worth between six to nine billion crowns.

- The eternal conflict about unemployment benefits seems to be over -- at least for the time being. The ruling Social Democrat party and union ferderation LO agreed to raise compensation levels to 80 percent from 75 percent of an unemployed worker's former wage. Payments will also be made once a month instead of once every two weeks.

- Sweden could be on the way to having a new share and options bourse if the Stockholm Stock Exchange and derivatives exchange OM Group merge. The government is expected to approve or reject the proposal in the next few weeks.
- Mining company Trelleborg, which said it would list its Boliden unit in Toronto, will use Canada as a springboard for Boliden's expansion into North and South America.
- Medical and industrial gas company AGA's managing director Lennart Selander says the company is facing tough years because of heavy investments in new projects, markets and plants.

- Some major manufacturers should consider moving their corporate headquarters abroad, according to Tom Hedelius, board chairman of Handelsbanken. He said he would conduct an unprejudiced appraisal of some of the firms in which he is involved. He is vice-chairman of telecoms group Ericsson, and of gas company AGA. He sits on the boards of forestry group SCA and AB Volvo.

- Swedish mining and rubber group Trelleborg AB said on Wednesday that it was moving its mining and metals company Boliden to Toronto, Canada. About 50 percent of Trelleborg's holding in Boliden will be offered in a public flotation primarily directed towards Canadian investors.

- Swedish Match alleges that the Social Welfare Board is dragging its heels in doing away with a requirement for labels on containers of moist tobacco snuff which warn it can cause cancer. Last week the Institute of Environmental Medicine released a report based on several research projects which concluded there is no basis for the claim that moist stuff causes cancer. In the meantime, Swedish Match is preparing to take its case to the European court.

- The Swedish Finance Inspectorate is for the first time investigating a case involving the illegal manipulation of share prices, an offence punishable by a maximum two years prison term. Bengt Tynell of the Finance Inspectorate said the investigation would be handled like a case of insider trading with no parties identified until inquiries were completed.
